Why product teams need sharper technical writing

Strong technical writing compresses ambiguity, lowers coordination cost, and preserves decisions longer than chat fragments.

Teams that write clearly tend to scope better, hand work across functions more cleanly, and spot contradictions earlier.

In product orgs, the quality of memos often predicts roadmap quality because weak reasoning hides inside vague prose.

When leaders force precision around assumptions, tradeoffs, and evidence, teams build fewer vanity features and ship less reactive work.

That does not require essays for everything. It requires durable artifacts where important thinking can be inspected and challenged.

Extensions like Sift benefit from the same discipline because selector strategy, privacy limits, and failure modes need explicit reasoning.

Good writing is not decoration. It is infrastructure for better judgment.
